title: OCI Container Runtimes & CRI Architecture
summary: Master the Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface (CRI), containerd daemon configuration, low-level OCI runtimes (runc vs gVisor sandboxes), and cri-tools (crictl) node diagnostics.
learningObjectives: Diagnose container and Pod sandbox states directly on worker nodes using the crictl CLI without apiserver dependency.
Configure containerd registry mirrors, endpoints, and certs in /etc/containerd/certs.d for high-availability image pulling.
Isolate multi-tenant and untrusted workloads using sandboxed OCI runtimes (gVisor runsc) and Kubernetes RuntimeClasses.

curriculumModules.title: CRI Architecture: Kubelet, containerd & CRI gRPC Interface
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: The Container Runtime Interface (CRI) is a gRPC API that allows Kubelet to communicate with container runtimes (containerd, CRI-O) over a local Unix domain socket (e.g. /run/containerd/containerd.sock). CRI exposes two main services: RuntimeService (pod sandbox management, container lifecycle, exec, logs) and ImageService (image pull, list, inspect, remove).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: When troubleshooting a worker node experiencing apiserver disconnection or NotReady status, use crictl directly against the containerd socket to inspect PodSandbox status and diagnose runtime failures.

curriculumModules.title: Low-Level OCI Runtimes: runc vs. Sandboxed Runtimes (gVisor runsc)
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: While standard runc relies on Linux cgroups and namespaces sharing the host kernel, sandboxed runtimes like gVisor (runsc) intercept system calls in user space via a Sentry process, providing strong virtualization-like boundary isolation without heavy VM overhead.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Define a Kubernetes RuntimeClass with handler 'runsc' and assign runtimeClassName: gvisor on untrusted, external-facing, or multi-tenant Pods to prevent host kernel exploits.

curriculumModules.title: containerd Registry Mirrors & cri-tools (crictl) Node Diagnostics
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: containerd 1.7+ and 2.0+ manage registry mirrors and authentication via /etc/containerd/certs.d/<registry-host>/hosts.toml. Configuring internal registry pull-through caches accelerates image distribution and prevents external rate-limiting incidents.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy local registry mirror configurations pointing to Harbor or internal caching proxies with TLS client certificate validation and fallback upstream registries.

labs.title: Worker Node Pod Sandbox & Container Diagnostics with crictl
labs.scenario: A worker node lost apiserver connectivity, but workloads must be verified locally. Connect directly to the containerd CRI socket using crictl to inspect active Pod sandboxes, inspect container runtime metadata, examine CPU and memory consumption, and audit containerd runtime engine info.
labs.productionContext: In production SEV-1 incidents where the Kubernetes control plane is unreachable or etcd has lost quorum, SREs use crictl directly on worker nodes to diagnose node-level container failures.
objectives: List all active Pod sandboxes on the node with crictl pods
List running containers across all sandboxes with crictl ps
Inspect container sandbox runtime details with crictl inspect
Query real-time resource utilization with crictl stats
Audit containerd CRI configuration and runtimes with crictl info

steps.title: Query Active Pod Sandboxes
steps.instruction: Run `crictl pods` to inspect all active Pod sandboxes managed by containerd.

steps.instruction: Run `crictl ps` to inspect all running containers and their parent Pod IDs.

steps.title: Inspect Container Details
steps.instruction: Inspect container runtime details and sandbox metadata using `crictl inspect a1b2c3d4e5f6`.

steps.title: Audit Stats and Engine Configuration
steps.instruction: Audit CPU and memory utilization with `crictl stats` and containerd runtime configuration with `crictl info`.

labs.title: Securing Untrusted Workloads with gVisor Sandboxed RuntimeClass
labs.scenario: A multi-tenant SaaS application executes untrusted third-party user scripts. Running them with standard runc exposes the host kernel to privilege escalation. You must register a Kubernetes RuntimeClass named 'gvisor' using handler 'runsc' and deploy a hardened Pod 'untrusted-sandbox' referencing this runtime class.
labs.productionContext: Using sandboxed OCI runtimes (gVisor or Kata Containers) provides kernel-level fault isolation, guaranteeing that an untrusted workload breakout cannot compromise the host kernel.
objectives: Verify containerd supports runsc sandbox via crictl info
Create and apply a Kubernetes RuntimeClass named gvisor with handler runsc
Deploy Pod untrusted-sandbox referencing runtimeClassName: gvisor
Verify pod status is Running under sandboxed isolation
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: gvisor
handler: runsc

steps.title: Audit containerd Runtime Handlers
steps.instruction: Audit containerd runtime configuration to verify `runsc` is available.

steps.title: Register RuntimeClass for gVisor
steps.instruction: Apply the RuntimeClass manifest registering `gvisor` with handler `runsc`.
steps.commandHint:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: gvisor
handler: runsc
EOF

steps.title: Deploy Sandboxed Pod
steps.instruction: Deploy Pod `untrusted-sandbox` with `runtimeClassName: gvisor` in namespace `default`.
steps.commandHint:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: untrusted-sandbox
  namespace: default
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor
  containers:
  - name: sandbox-app
    image: nginx:1.27-alpine
EOF

steps.title: Verify Running Status
steps.instruction: Verify that `untrusted-sandbox` entered the `Running` phase under gVisor isolation.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does gVisor (runsc) fundamentally isolate container workloads compared to standard runc?
options: (Recommended) gVisor acts as an application kernel running in user space (Sentry), intercepting guest system calls and emulating them without direct access to the host kernel.
gVisor spins up a heavy full-weight VMware hypervisor virtual machine for each container.
gVisor uses standard Linux namespaces without any system call filtering or interception.
gVisor only works on Windows containers and cannot execute Linux ELF binaries.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Unlike runc which shares the host Linux kernel directly via cgroups and namespaces, gVisor provides a distinct application kernel (Sentry) implemented in Go that intercepts system calls and implements kernel primitives in user space, shielding the host kernel from exploits.

assessmentQuestions.question: In containerd 1.7+ and 2.0+, what is the recommended architecture for configuring private registry mirrors with TLS certificates?
options: Passing unencrypted plaintext flags to kubelet --image-repository-mirror.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: containerd uses the /etc/containerd/certs.d/ directory structure where each registry host has its own directory containing hosts.toml, CA certs, and client TLS credentials, providing decentralized, modular mirror and endpoint configuration.
